scope: buffered cached file I/O and explicit sync; not SSD throughput
method_notes: Same upstream fio 3.43, generic native-disabled builds and official --disable-shm option on both operating systems; no fio source modifications.
CONFIG_NO_SHM uses anonymous shared mmap instead of unimplemented guest SysV shmget. thread=1 and psync/depth=1 are identical for all variants.
kb_base=1000 gives IEC input sizes. Every measured byte count was checked against total_ios*4096 or total_ios*1048576.
Dataset: 256 MiB single-job file and four independent 64 MiB parallel files, 512 MiB per variant, 1.5 GiB total; same APFS volume.
Three independently shuffled rounds, 5 measured seconds plus 1 second ramp; successful jobs, completed byte counts, runtimes and raw fio JSON checked.
All writes end with explicit full synchronization. Reported write bandwidth can include final-drain cost and is not pure memory-copy bandwidth.
No cache eviction or genuine guest O_DIRECT: host direct probe succeeds, private/shared probes both return EINVAL (22). Cached reads are not physical SSD bandwidth.
Linux disk_util is disabled; native macOS fio does not implement that sampler. Clock source is clock_gettime on both sides.
fio on macOS uses F_FULLFSYNC for fsync; Trames Rust File::sync_all also uses F_FULLFSYNC, with private namespace persistence in addition.
fdatasync is a diagnostic, not equal host durability semantics: native fio calls macOS fdatasync; guest sync_data uses Apple Rust F_FULLFSYNC and private namespace checkpoint.
Existing Stable/Dev guests were not stopped or reconfigured. The isolated benchmark service was stopped, datasets removed, free space returned to about 31 GiB.
Other desktop/services remained running. Read/4 KiB results are stable across these samples, but sequential end-synced write results have wide ranges.
Guest fio CPU usage fields are currently zero and cannot support host-vs-guest CPU utilization conclusions.
No native Linux VM result was collected in this fio run; all host references are native macOS.

Tool preparation installed make (about 452 kB package download) into the existing Dev Debian; its dedicated /tmp build directory was removed after extracting the benchmark binary. No existing environment was restarted.
